requirements.title: LLT argument restrictions
requirements.definition: STRING_A shall be default character or ASCII character, and STRING_B shall be character with the same kind type parameter as STRING_A.

pending.LLT-STRING_A-default-or-ASCII-character: Positive source controls call LLT with default CHARACTER STRING_A and same-kind character STRING_B; source-control mutations use a noncharacter actual and claim no diagnostic facet.
pending.LLT-STRING_B-same-character-kind: Positive source controls call LLT with same-kind default CHARACTER arguments; a source-control mutation uses different character kinds and claims no diagnostic facet.

requirements.title: LLT uses blank padding and ASCII less-than result semantics
requirements.definition: For ASCII strings, unequal lengths are compared after right blank padding of the shorter string; LLT is true exactly for STRING_A preceding STRING_B in the ASCII collating sequence, and false otherwise.

pending.LLT-unequal-length-blank-padding: Initialize logical results to opposite sentinels and assert LLT("A","A!") is true while LLT("A","A ") is false, proving right blank padding and ASCII order are both load-bearing; mutate the second operand punctuation or intrinsic name to LLE so one assertion fails.
pending.LLT-ascii-precedes-true: Assert ASCII-table discriminators with .false. sentinels: LLT("9","A") is true because ASCII 57 precedes 65, LLT("A","a") is true because ASCII 65 precedes 97, LLT("Z","a") is true because ASCII 90 precedes 97, and LLT("Z","_") is true because ASCII 90 precedes 95. Also retain LLT("ONE","TWO") as the example-derived same-case control. Reverse each discriminator in companion false checks so ASCII collating sequence, not native character order, is load-bearing.
pending.LLT-equal-strings-false: Assert LLT("AZ","AZ") and LLT("","") are false with .true. sentinels; mutate LLT to LLE so equality becomes true.
pending.LLT-ascii-follows-false: Assert reversed ASCII-table discriminators with .true. sentinels: LLT("A","9") is false because ASCII 65 follows 57, LLT("a","A") is false because ASCII 97 follows 65, LLT("a","Z") is false because ASCII 97 follows 90, and LLT("_","Z") is false because ASCII 95 follows 90. Also assert LLT("B","A") is false as a same-case control; swap operands so each false case becomes true.

requirements.title: LLT non-ASCII comparison result is processor dependent
requirements.definition: A LLT comparison result is processor dependent once either string contains a character outside the ASCII character set.

pending.LLT-non-ASCII-result-processor-dependent: No portable oracle for a fixed truth value: p5 makes any result processor dependent once either string contains a non-ASCII character; future exact LLT fixtures restrict operands to ASCII characters.
